title: pm-dispatch: set effort by the official criteria — xhigh only for long hardest builds and high-severity security fixes
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

Filing gate ③: maintainer-directed task. Ruling-ref: the maintainer said 「立卡修改skills」 (2026-11-19, seat 5 thread) after the effort review, and 「安全修复只有高风险的才需要 xhigh 吧」 then 「目前的安全卡非常多，按照这个标准是不是很烧钱，有没有更好的方案」 on security. ⛔ Not a claim. Not part of epic #35205; overlap-check its open step PRs before branching (same files).

Analysis (read-only, contract tier, against `origin/main` @ `f4dbcc2153` and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort): project file `objectstack-seat5/effort-policy-review.md`.

## Why

Today `xhigh` fires by category (`execution-duties.md:128`: XL / security / epic sub-card / L2 review / four-axis analysis / ADR). The official guidance for the current models fires it by shape instead: long autonomous runs (over 30 minutes, very large token budgets) and only where a sweep measured a gain; the contract tier is told to start at `high`. "Unsure, raise one level" (`:130`) runs opposite to the guidance (raise on measured gain, lower when quality holds). The `security` label alone sends dependency bumps, permission-page UX and copy cards to `xhigh`.

## What to do

Line numbers are at `f4dbcc2153`; re-read before editing. Tier words only, no model ids.

1. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md`
   - `:128` → `xhigh` only for builds expected to run unattended over 30 minutes (XL usually), or a card type a sweep record shows gains at `xhigh`. Epic sub-card, ADR and p1 go by the card's own difficulty; a category ⛔ never raises a level. L2 review, four-axis analysis, design and red-line re-read subagents run at `high`. `max` on a named or standing order, or to test the ceiling.
   - Security (seat proposal answering the maintainer's cost question, confirm before landing): grade by consequence, not label. Only an advisory graded high severity (cross-tenant or unauthorised read/write, privilege escalation, auth bypass) earns `xhigh`, and then not for the whole build: build at `high`, then one read-only subagent at `xhigh` does a short adversarial review of the diff. Medium severity → `high`. `security`-labelled cards that are not advisory fixes (deps, UX, copy) → by difficulty. Every security fix carries a regression test that reproduces the attack: fails before the fix, passes after. Fixes sharing one mechanism share one analysis.
   - `:129` → card threads fixed at open; ⛔ never change session effort mid-session (it drops the cache); a different level goes to an isolated subagent.
   - `:130` → unsure ⇒ `high`, ⛔ never `xhigh` on doubt. Add: read-only lookup/fetch helper subagents floor `medium`, a single-shot lookup may use `low`, a long check chain ⛔ never `low`. Effort values come from this repo's sweeps, ⛔ not carried over from an older model generation; re-sweep when a tier changes generation and log the readings on a record card.
   - `:104` ADR-revision standing order `xhigh` → `high`. ⛔ Standing order: change only with the maintainer's own word in the PR's Ruling-ref; otherwise leave the line and say so in the PR.
2. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/l2-review.md:7` → the per-head contract-tier subagent is passed `high`.
3. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md:39` → seat sessions stay `high` and ⛔ never change mid-session.
4. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/security-findings.md:27` → align with the security rule in 1 (high severity: `high` build + `xhigh` diff review).
5. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:321` claim-line effort field → an `xhigh` value cites its duration reading or sweep record on the same line. Protocol-semantic face.
6. `.claude/skills/checklist-test/SKILL.md:107` → adversarial re-review of a disputed verdict at `high`; `xhigh` only per the security rule in 1.

## Sweeps (before, or in the same PR as, the L2 and security lines)

- Review sweep: 5 old L2 heads with real findings, read-only subagent at `high` vs `xhigh`, 3 runs each. Read recall of the known findings, false findings, tokens, minutes. If recall drops at `high`, the L2 line keeps `xhigh`.
- Security sweep: 3–5 merged security fixes re-run at `high` from their base. If the same fix and test come out, the high-severity diff review drops to `high` too.
- Build sweep: 6 merged cards (S/M/L ×2) re-run at `medium`/`high` (L also `xhigh`); read first-push gate pass, L1 rework rounds, tokens, minutes.
- Record readings on one record card; no cost estimate without them.

## Done when

The rule lines above say what this card says (or the PR names each line left as is and why), the sweep readings are recorded, the skill gates pass, and the PR carries a contract review (governed `.claude/**`, `SKILL.md` is a protocol-semantic face). Seat 5 reviews and lands.
